title: NetCL: A Unified Programming Framework for In-Network Computing
problem: Programmable data planes for in-network computing require deep networking expertise and P4 DSL knowledge, limiting accessibility. INC programmers must think in networking terms rather than computational abstractions to articulate their tasks.
motivation: Making in-network computing accessible to general programmers rather than just network specialists could enable broader adoption of this emerging computational paradigm.
method: NetCL lets you write in-network computing (code that processes data inside network switches) using C/C++ and special APIs for this task. You write simple programs called kernels that process data packets as they travel through the network. A compiler automatically translates your kernels into P4 code (the language network switches use), and a lightweight runtime handles low-level networking details.
key_novelty: NetCL enables ordinary programmers to write in-network computing (code that processes data inside network switches) using C/C++ with automatic compilation to P4, eliminating the need for specialized networking expertise.
contributions: C/C++ extensions for expressing INC as kernel functions processing in-flight messages
Compiler that translates INC kernels to P4 code
Thin runtime system abstracting network plumbing details
